Deep monitors

Checks that reach into the appliance — a synthetic HTTPS request to a published service, interface IP/link drift, processor load, memory usage and the proxyd daemon — each stored as a time series with its own thresholds.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereMonitoring → Deep monitors (every ADOM) (URL /monitoring/deep/)

What is it?#

Deep monitors answers is the service actually serving? Each probe either sends a synthetic request through the published front end, reads the device's interfaces from SATOM's cache, or runs a read-only CLI command on the appliance. Results are stored as time series because the interesting signal is usually a value changing — an IP that moved, a daemon that restarted.

All probe mechanics (discover, add, mute, charts, statuses, retention) are shared with Service Monitor and described in Probes.

What does it do?#

Kind (Type in the form) What it records Products
Service policy (HTTPS) HTTP status, latency and days left on the served TLS certificate for a URL. A sweep sends these requests concurrently (up to 16 at a time); a front end that refuses or times out the connection is not contacted again for its certificate any — it calls a URL and needs no device API
Interface IP / link a fingerprint of every watched port's address and state; a change against the previous sample is the event FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer
Processor load CPU busy % FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator
Memory usage memory used % FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator
proxyd process worker count, box memory consumed and free, and the set of process IDs; a changed set is a silent restart FortiWeb

Data sources:

  • Interface reads the device cache refreshed by the hourly device_sync, so drift is detected at harvest cadence and the probe works with the appliance off.
  • Processor load / Memory usage run get system performance over the read-only CLI on FortiWeb and FortiADC; on FortiAuthenticator they read /api/v1/systeminfo/ over REST, because its CLI answers No such command.
  • proxyd runs diagnose system top. It reports box memory consumed and free, never the daemon's %VSZ.

Requirements#

  • See Probes → Requirements (the deep_monitor sweep).
  • SSH access configured on the appliance for the CLI kinds.
  • A recent harvest for the interface kind (device_sync).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Same as Probes: reading needs the legacy view gate (any read permission, for example monitoring.view); changing or running probes needs the legacy config_write gate, e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: opening Deep monitors now requires a read permission instead of sign-in alone, and new probes default to a 3-minute interval.

How to use#

Discover from a device#

Discover from device offers three sets on this page. Everything is read from the harvest cache, so it works with the appliance powered off.

Set Creates
Server policies one HTTPS probe per published front end (explicit IP → system VIP → bound interface). FortiWeb only
Device baseline one interface watch covering all ports, processor load and memory usage, plus proxyd on FortiWeb (only the kinds the product supports)
One probe per interface a separate probe, series and history for every port

Changed on 2026-10-14. Server policies dials each new front end once before it creates the probe. When SATOM cannot connect to the VIP (nothing routes it from SATOM's network, the connection is refused, or TLS fails before a session), the probe is created disabled. Its Last result explains why, and the job message counts these probes as "created disabled: VIP not reachable from SATOM". A disabled probe does not count in Device health. Enable it once SATOM can reach the VIP. A front end that connects but answers badly (a timeout after connecting, HTTP 5xx) is created enabled, because that is a finding about the service. Policies that are disabled on the device are not dialled.

You do not need Discover to get the device baseline. It is created when the device is added, from the form, the REST API or a provisioning run, and the 3-minute Collection sweep also gives it to any device that still has no probe. A probe you delete on a provisioned device stays deleted. To stop monitoring a device completely, disable its probes rather than deleting them all.

Add a probe by hand#

Click Add probe, choose the Type, and fill the fields below. See Probes → How to use for the common steps.

Configuration#

Field Kind Description Required Example
URL Service policy (HTTPS) Full URL to request Yes https://192.0.2.10:443/
Expect status HTTPS Exact status expected; 0 = any < 400 No 200
Slow above (ms) HTTPS Latency that grades warn No (inherits) 2000
TLS warn (days) HTTPS Certificate runway that grades warn; expired is crit No (inherits) 21
Ports to watch Interface Nothing ticked = every port as one series; tick a subset to watch only those No port1, port2
Warn if the harvest is older than (hours) Interface Cache age that grades warn No (inherits) 6
Process proxyd Process name, matched on the command basename Yes proxyd
Warn at % / Critical at % Processor load, Memory usage Levels; 0 disables a level No (inherits) 80 / 95

How each kind is graded#

  • HTTPS — unreachable, no status, or a status ≥ 400 (or different from Expect status) is crit; an expired certificate is crit; slow or short certificate runway is warn.
  • Interface — a watched port missing from the cache, or an address change, is graded by its binary fact (default crit); a port down, another change, or a stale harvest is warn; an empty cache is error (no interfaces in the device cache — run a device sync).
  • Processor load / Memory usage — against Warn at % / Critical at %. A command that returns no reading is error.
  • proxyd — not running is graded by its fact (default crit); a changed PID set by its fact (default warn).

Example#

🧪Example — Know when the shop front end stops answering

  1. Add probe → Type Service policy (HTTPS) → Name shop front end → Device fweb-01 → URL https://shop.example.com/ → Expect status 200.
  2. Save. On the next sweep the row shows status, latency and certificate days.
  3. If the VIP stops answering, the probe turns crit, the device badge on Device health turns critical, and the alert engine mails it (if enabled).

Result#

See Probes → Result. HTTPS probes also store response headers, body length and the error text in the sample payload (visible in History).

Troubleshooting#

"no interfaces in the device cache — run a device sync"#

The device has never been harvested or its cache is empty. Run a rediscovery or wait for device_sync.

"get system performance returned no CPU reading …"#

The CLI answered without a value (wrong product, or unparsable output). Check the device's SSH access; on FortiAuthenticator the probe reads REST instead.

"could not parse diagnose system top output"#

The raw response is kept in the sample payload; open History → Latest raw payload to see it.

Interface probe is "warn: harvest is stale — device_sync may be failing"#

The cache is older than the probe's limit. Fix the harvest (see Device health).

HTTPS probe "unreachable: …"#

SATOM's own network path cannot reach the URL. That is a statement about the path from the SATOM node, which may differ from the appliance's path. Use Path Diagnostics to localise the failing layer.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • The HTTPS kind requests any URL you enter; it is not limited to inventory hosts.
  • The interface target field holds at most 120 characters of port names; a list that does not fit drops whole names at the end rather than truncating a name.
  • The REST-telemetry kinds (sessions, throughput, transactions, licence, tokens) live on Service Monitor. The two pages share one sweep, so do not schedule a second one.
#deep monitor#https probe#synthetic request#interface drift#cpu#memory#proxyd#restart detection#tls expiry
